cases.name: separate-skill-value-from-native-integration
cases.trap: Collapse two different claims into one test: treat native loading as proof the methodology helps, or treat an ablation response as proof production roles really load companion methodology.
cases.prompt: A new incident-triage skill has two unresolved questions before broad rollout. First, maintainers want evidence that its evidence-triage method improves decisions compared with the model unaided. Second, a production regression suggests Reviewer sometimes skips the skill's ASSESSMENT companion even when the skill is relevant. Design the minimum evaluation coverage for both questions without conflating what each result proves.
expectations: Separates the two claims instead of trying to prove both with one case.

Uses a skill-owned baseline/candidate ablation case for whether incident-triage materially improves the model's reasoning, with the same task on both sides and only the candidate receiving the target skill.
Uses a central runtime native-integration case for whether production Reviewer actually loads the skill and consumes its assessment path.
For the ablation case, requires absolute candidate correctness while preserving baseline-to-candidate delta as skill-value evidence rather than PASS by improvement alone.
For the runtime integration case, requires observed skill loading and assessment action bound to incident-triage rather than accepting final prose as proof.
States that an ablation result does not prove production integration and a native load does not prove the methodology adds value.
negative_expectations: Must not use presence of a skill tool call as the primary proof that the skill improves reasoning.
Must not claim a reasoning-only candidate response proves Reviewer consumed the companion in production.
Must not give the ablation candidate extra task hints beyond the target skill.

cases.name: choose-runtime-for-native-skill-integration
cases.trap: Use reasoning-only ablation to claim that a production Reviewer really loaded and consumed companion methodology.
cases.prompt: A regression report says Reviewer sometimes reviews Go work without actually loading the relevant skill assessment companion. The behavior we need to prove is production integration: Reviewer must natively load the skill and invoke the Loom assessment path for that skill. Design the focused eval.
expectations: Chooses a central native skill integration case, normally in evals/skills.json, rather than a skill-owned ablation case.
Uses runtime execution with the OpenCode target because the claim depends on real production skill/tool behavior.
Requires observed native skill loading and the relevant loom_assessment action bound to the intended skill, rather than inferring use from final prose.
Keeps the scenario realistic and checks the production behavior without teaching the target the harness assertion.
Explains that this proves native integration, not that the skill itself materially improves reasoning quality.
negative_expectations: Must not claim that a reasoning-only candidate response proves native production loading.
Must not accept a final answer that merely says the skill was used as sufficient integration evidence.
